answer: An agent marketplace requires every identity to lock a refundable bond before bidding, with one bond per concurrent bidder. Agents named harbor, vertex, and quill face the same rule: funds stay locked until their bids expire or their jobs finish. An attacker can still create a thousand identities, but activating them requires a thousand bonds. Reusing the same capital forces the attacker to wait, making a swarm costly to run at scale.
